title: Oppenheimer Says AI Software Spending Is Shifting Towards Measurable Returns
key_facts: Oppenheimer says enterprise AI spending is moving from experimentation to focus on return on investment
AI is becoming a recurring operating expense, with CFOs assessing it alongside labour costs
Value creation is moving further up the IT stack
Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce and ServiceNow each have AI businesses above USD 1 billion, per Oppenheimer
Workday is recording high AI attach rates
Oppenheimer is cautious on Figma and SoundHound AI
quote_evidence: Oppenheimer said enterprise artificial intelligence spending is moving from an experimentation phase towards a greater focus on return on investment.
why_it_matters_hint: Buyers want proof of returns before they add AI spending.
notes: Yahoo Finance page has no named author or Oppenheimer link; credited as Yahoo Finance citing Oppenheimer. Google News also lists an Oppenheimer "top software application stocks" item dated 28 Sep 2026 (Investing.com), which may be related earlier coverage; not confirmed to be the same note. Article names stocks Oppenheimer prefers or is wary of (Microsoft, ServiceNow, Braze; Figma and SoundHound cautious): these are the firm's views, not ours, and no buy or sell advice is given here.
